thesis_narrative: SaaS company trading at 22x forward earnings despite 25% revenue growth and 75% gross margins. The discount exists because of a one-time customer churn event in Q3 that spooked short-term holders. Retention metrics (NRR 115%) show the churn was concentrated in one vertical. At $180 fair value vs $140 current price, the 22% discount offers a margin of safety with growth doing the heavy lifting. Key risk: if NRR drops below 110%, the growth narrative breaks.

Regional bank trading at 0.9x tangible book value while peers trade at 1.3x. NIM of 3.4% is above median. Credit quality is clean with NPL ratio at 0.4%. The discount stems from CRE exposure concerns, but the portfolio is 80% multifamily with low LTV. At $42 fair value vs $34 current, the 19% discount provides downside protection. Dividend yield of 3.2% provides income while waiting. Key risk: commercial real estate deterioration beyond multifamily.

Specialty distributor with 15% ROIC and sticky customer relationships (95% retention). Trading at 14x earnings, a 30% discount to sector median of 20x. The discount reflects cyclical fears, but 60% of revenue is aftermarket/recurring. Book-to-bill at 1.1x signals continued demand. At $85 fair value vs $62 current, the 27% discount anchors the thesis. Key risk: if the industrial cycle turns sharply, even recurring revenue faces pressure.
